Grodzisk Mazowiecki Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Grodzisk Mazowiecki, Poland

Not demolished. Grodzisk Mazowiecki's Jewish community, established in the 18th century, once made up 87 percent of the town's population in 1808, before declining proportionally to about 25 percent by 1921 even as its absolute numbers grew; in 1941 the Germans deported the community to the Warsaw Ghetto, and most were later killed at Treblinka. This cemetery, established in the second half of the 18th century and expanded repeatedly through 1934, was the site of German executions during WWII and suffered gradual postwar destruction — postwar authorities handed much of it to a farming cooperative and later a scrapyard, and even a 1988 restoration effort was partly undone when the municipality demolished part of the fence in 2016. About 200 tombstones survive today within a fenced 0.28-hectare section maintained since 2009 by local volunteers, though legal proceedings to establish clear ownership of the land remain unresolved.
